## What to Consider

LiveKit is a go-to choice for teams that want an infrastructure-first, WebRTC-native platform to build highly customized real-time audio/video experiences. The alternatives split into distinct camps: Daily positions itself as a batteries-included calling + streaming/recording platform with a growing AI voice-agent story (Pipecat) and telephony/SIP connectivity, while 100ms emphasizes proven stability under demanding, high-concurrency workloads. Dyte differentiates with rapid time-to-production and a plugin-driven approach backed by notably high-touch support, whereas Whereby optimizes for the simplest possible “click a link and join” meeting experience; Tencent RTC represents the large-vendor, cloud-managed RTC option. [...] Learn more →

Tencent RTC fits teams that want a cloud-managed RTC backend from a large vendor with broad platform coverage. As an alternative to LiveKit’s more infrastructure-builder mindset, Tencent RTC is typically considered when the goal is to rely on a managed service rather than operating and tuning real-time systems directly.

It can be a sensible choice for products that value vendor ecosystem alignment, procurement familiarity, and consolidated cloud relationships. For enterprise contexts or multi-region deployments, that “big cloud provider” posture can simplify governance and reduce the number of separate vendors involved.

# Best LiveKit Alternatives in 2026

Open-source WebRTC infrastructure for video, audio, and data

## What is LiveKit?

LiveKit is an open-source WebRTC platform that handles the hard parts of real-time communication: video, audio, screen sharing, and data channels. Instead of wrestling with STUN/TURN servers, codec negotiation, and bandwidth estimation yourself, you point LiveKit's SDK at a room and it handles the rest. It supports SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit) architecture, which scales far better than peer-to-peer for group calls. [...] What sets LiveKit apart in 2026 is its AI agent framework. You can build voice-based AI agents that join rooms as participants, think AI customer support reps, interview bots, or real-time translation layers. The Agents framework handles speech-to-text, LLM processing, and text-to-speech in a pipeline with low enough latency to feel conversational.

You can self-host LiveKit for free (Apache 2.0) or use LiveKit Cloud. Key pricing change in 2026: upstream bandwidth is now free, and downstream rates dropped from $0.18/GB to $0.12/GB, specifically benefiting voice AI workloads. Cloud plans: Build (free, 1,000 agent minutes/mo), Ship ($50/mo), Scale ($500/mo), Enterprise (custom). Agent Session Minutes cost $0.01/min.
